audit.why: Full phases[].side, content win[] and the packet levelChart all agree: Karma rows 0-5, Kassadin at 2+ items. Karma's 950-range Q against a 650-range mana-gated melee mage is a real lane edge; the 45.45% win rate over 44 games reflects the late game, not the lane, and the chart's final row already hands that to Kassadin.
audit.corrected: Chart left alone; the packet defect flag is a win-rate-vs-chart heuristic and the chart is defensible here.

audit.why: Riftwalk drops from 5s at rank 1 to 2s at rank 3, so the spike that decides the matchup is level 16, not level 6 — the spikes[] entries already describe scaling, they just lacked the numbers.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns and the snowball lines so the scaling deadline is concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page states that Null Sphere shields Kassadin as it casts, or that Nether Blade is an auto-attack reset on a 7s cooldown.
audit.why: Both are in Riot's text/flags and both change how you spend your first chunk of damage.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere's shield is called out in report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns; the Nether Blade wind-up tell is in phases[3].why.
sources: enemyKit Q shield flag and text

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT); dosFull[2].d invented a 'fifteen-second' Riftwalk cooldown.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2 seconds. Fifteen is not close to any number in the kit.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns written: Riftwalk 5s/2s, Force Pulse 21s at rank 1, Null Sphere 9s, and the invented figure removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two copy-paste-bleed bullets (dosFull[1].d = tradeGood, dontsFull[2].d = tradeBad).

audit.corrected: Both replaced with bodies that answer their own titles.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to 16, then chaining 2-second Riftwalks onto you while Null Sphere's shield eats the first chunk you land.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Count it out loud if you must. - Your RE shield-speed has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 but only 2s at rank 3 — past 16 you never catch him, so bill the lane before then. - Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1 and needs charges; spent, he cannot slow your exit. - Null Sphere is 9s and shields him as it casts.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — the RQ chunk cycles every 30 seconds. Chip him below half and hold the kill window.
edits.after: Lost Chapter timing — his Nether Blade wind-up is a 7s tell: step out of it, then RQ him below half.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, and on real windows RQ-W: the chunk plus tether-root turns a poke trade into a kill setup — E out before the answer.
edits.after: When he blinks in, RE for the shield and speed, then W — the 675 tether holds him in Q range while each extra Riftwalk costs him more mana.

edits.before: Kassadin burns Riftwalk on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Kassadin blinks to dodge a Q — he is out of position, and it returns in 5s.

edits.before: That’s Kassadin’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Past two items his blink chains faster than your flat 12s W — shield and root for others.

edits.before: Spending Mantra on wave-clear while behind on poke — Karma without RQ banked is a support who took mid's farm.
edits.after: With Inspire down you have no speed to leave, and his 400-range Force Pulse cone slows you into whatever walks out of river.

edits.before: Carry early or enable late — RQ chips win lanes; RE + roots win the teamfights your early lead bought.
edits.after: Carry early or enable late — RQ chips him off CS; once he blinks every 2s your job is shields and roots.

edits.before: Ahead, sprint: RQ Kassadin off every wave, take plates with the lead, and W-root river picks — Karma leads are sprints, not marathons.
edits.after: Ahead, sprint: RQ him off the wave, take plates, and roam on RE speed — minutes you steal are minutes he cannot spend scaling toward 16.

edits.before: Ahead, sprint: RQ Kassadin off every wave, take plates with the lead, and W-root river picks — Karma leads are sprints, not marathons.
edits.after: Ahead, sprint: RQ him off the wave, take plates, and roam on RE speed — minutes you steal are minutes he cannot spend scaling toward 16.

edits.before: Track Kassadin’s Riftwalk: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Null Sphere shields him as it casts, so his Q eats your first chunk — bait it out, then W while Riftwalk is still 5s.

notes: The packet flags 'level chart contradicts data: Karma wins only 45.45% but the chart gives Karma 6/7 stages'. Left the chart alone deliberately: all three sources (full sides, content win[], packet chart) already agree, and a lane-dominant / late-losing shape is exactly what a sub-50% Karma vs Kassadin record looks like at 44 games. Flag conflict: the kit marks Kassadin's Null Sphere with a 'channel: interruptible' flag, but Riot's own description says the spell INTERRUPTS channels — it is not itself a channel. Per the calibration rule I trusted the description and did NOT write that your W or Mantra cancels his Q. Kassadin is male; no misgender findings.
